deep.reconstruction:
Context: the folder 'Champs 1' and the previous page, which lists (Ss Unités) -> (Cat) <-> (Prédériv) -> (Ord) -> (Maquettes). The previous page also has drawings of subdivided segments and of lens-shaped 2-cells pasted in rows and in grids.

The page does three things.

(1) It writes down the data of a 2-category or bicategory.
- A 2-globular set F_0 <= F_1 <= F_2, with source and target maps s_1,t_1 : F_1 -> F_0 and s_2,t_2 : F_2 -> F_1.
- Identity (degeneracy) maps σ_1 : F_0 -> F_1 and σ_2 : F_1 -> F_2.
- Three compositions: μ^1_1 composes 1-cells over a 0-cell; μ^2_1 composes 2-cells horizontally over a 0-cell; μ^2_2 composes 2-cells vertically over a 1-cell.
- The constraints a, l, r (associator, left unitor, right unitor). The line I_A∘S -> S is the left unit constraint for a 1-cell S with source or target A.
- The pictures are the standard ones: segments subdivided into composable 1-cells; lenses (globes) as 2-cells; rows of lenses for horizontal composition; stacked lenses for vertical composition; 2x2 grids for interchange.

(2) It studies how a product of simplices Δ_{n1}×...×Δ_{nr} (in particular Δ_n×Δ_{n'}) becomes a globular pasting diagram.
- The bottom drawings show a horizontal path of 4 arrows times a vertical arrow.
- This gives a grid of squares carrying horizontal 1-cells and vertical double-arrow 2-cells.
- Collapsing the vertical edges turns the grid into a chain of 4 lenses. Each lens is subdivided into stacked 2-cells pointing downward.
- So the bidimensional poset Δ_n×Δ_{n'} is converted into a 2-globular set:
  - F_0 = Ob Δ_n (the pinch points),
  - F_1 = Fl(Δ_n) × Ob Δ_{n'} (the horizontal arrows at each level),
  - F_2 = Fl(Δ_n) × Fl(Δ_{n'}) (the vertical arrows between levels, fibred over a horizontal arrow).
- Source and target of a 2-cell (f,u) are (f, s u) and (f, t u).

(3) The next page generalises this to categories C_1,...,C_n. There F_k = Fl C_1 × ... × Fl C_k × Ob C_{k+1}, which gives an n-globular set built from an n-fold product. The verso and the next page also give the globe/cylinder construction (F×I) ⊔_{Ḟ×I} Ḟ for Ḟ ⊂ F. This is the cylinder with its boundary collapsed, which produces the next-dimensional globe (a lens) from a disk with boundary.

What it serves: building 'models' (maquettes, previous page) of higher pasting shapes for a theory of n-stacks or n-categories. Products of ordinals are turned into globular shapes, very much in the spirit of Pursuing Stacks.
errors: The globular set F_0=Ob Δ_n, F_1=Fl Δ_n×Ob Δ_{n'}, F_2=Fl Δ_n×Fl Δ_{n'} is not closed under horizontal composition: (f,u) and (g,u') with u≠u' share a 0-cell but have no composite in F. It is a globular set, or the generating pasting scheme, not itself a 2-category. The 2-category it generates is the Θ_2-cell [n]([n'],...,[n']), whose hom(i,j) is [n']^{j-i}, not [n'].
Index slips: F_2 is written with Δ_{n''}, but F_1 and the drawing require Δ_{n'}. F_0 is written with the index n', but consistency with F_1 requires Ob Δ_n.
The page is a sketch: the axioms (interchange, coherence for a, l, r) are only pictured, not stated.

ideas.what: Presentation of a bicategory/2-category by a 2-globular set with sources/targets, identities σ_i, compositions μ^1_1, μ^2_1, μ^2_2 and constraints a, l, r
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) uses globular sets and composition/coherence data

ideas.what: Turning a product of ordinals Δ_n×Δ_{n'} (and more generally C_1×...×C_n) into a globular pasting shape by collapsing transversal edges: F_k = Fl C_1×...×Fl C_k×Ob C_{k+1}
ideas.modern_name: the functor Δ×Θ_{n-1} -> Θ_n, ([m],c) ↦ [m](c,...,c); wreath product Δ≀Θ_{n-1}; 'suspension' of multisimplicial shapes to Θ-cells
ideas.where_published: Not as such; Pursuing Stacks discusses globular 'models' and test categories but I do not recall this product-collapse formula

ideas.what: Globe/cylinder construction (F×I) ⊔_{Ḟ×I} Ḟ giving the next-dimensional globe from a disk with boundary
ideas.modern_name: reduced cylinder / globular suspension (D^{n+1} from D^n×I with ∂D^n×I collapsed)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; standard in globular homotopy theory (Batanin, Street, Ara–Métayer)

ideas.what: Drawings comparing grids of squares (cubical/multisimplicial pasting) with chains of lenses (globular pasting), including interchange
ideas.modern_name: cubical vs globular pasting; Gray-type products

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly maps products of ordinals (multisimplices Δ_{n1}×...×Δ_{nr}, or products of categories) to globular pasting shapes, with k-cells Fl C_1×...×Fl C_k×Ob C_{k+1}. This is essentially the Δ^r -> Θ_r / Δ×Θ_{n-1} -> Θ_n comparison used much later (Joyal, Berger, Bergner–Rezk). The notes appear to date from the Pursuing Stacks / Dérivateurs period, well before those works.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the idea of comparing multisimplicial and Θ/globular shapes. Mathematically the construction is now standard, and the sketch is incomplete (it does not even form a 2-category without closure).

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine bicategory and pasting doodles. The mildly notable part is an early, explicit recipe that collapses products of simplices or categories into globular cells, anticipating the Θ-cell / wreath-product comparison. It is only sketched, so the interest is historical rather than mathematical.
transcription_corrections: 'F_0 = ∂Δ_{n'}' should read 'F_0 = Ob Δ_n': the handwritten 'ob' was misread as ∂ / 'δ3'.
'F_1 = Fl(Δ_n)×∂Δ_{n'}' should read 'F_1 = Fl(Δ_n)×Ob Δ_{n'}'; the struck-out word is an aborted 'Ob Δ_n'.
'F_2 = Fl(Δ_n)×Fl(Δ_{n''})': the second factor is most likely Fl(Δ_{n'}).
The superscript on the first μ looks like '4' but is μ^1_1.
'Δ_{n1}×Δ_{n2}×...×Δ_{nr}' is written with arrows ('×←–←') in the original, possibly indicating projections or a tower.
